solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crazed stabber cuts seat without thinking, OK

indicators.note: a crazed thing is out of its right mind, so the following word's letters lose their order
to cut something is to go into it, so the jumbled letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: the rump is the backside one sits on
taken as written, ready to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A maniac with a knife slashes a seat cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without thinking, OK' reads as a comment on the stabbing, but it is the definition: a verb, to approve automatically.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubber-stamp a proposal is to approve it automatically, giving official assent with no real scrutiny.

clue.text: Nasty persons spreading bile are to blame

indicators.note: something nasty has been made unpleasant and disordered, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unpleasant people who spread venom are at fault for the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' only joins the two fodder words in the surface; 'Nasty' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held responsible for a mishap means being the one at fault, the party deserving censure for it.

clue.text: Plaintively express line in rhythm

indicators.note: one item placed in another means it sits within that word's letters

blocks.note: a beat is the pulse of music
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A poet voices a lament with a single line set to a rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleat is to speak in a weak, complaining voice, like a sheep's cry, hence to express something plaintively.

clue.text: Hold top off barrier to let rising sun in

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, and taking it off removes that letter
in a down entry something rising reads from bottom to top, so it is turned around
letting something in means admitting it inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a fence is a barrier round a field
Sol is the Latin name for the sun

explanation.surface: Remove the top rail of a fence so the morning sun can shine through.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light the top is the first letter and rising reads upwards. Sol is the sun in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose something is to contain or surround it, so a box can be said to hold what it encloses.

clue.text: Active ace removed from jet

indicators.note: something removed from a word is taken out of it, leaving the other letters

blocks.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
a jet of water is a spray

explanation.surface: A star pilot is taken off the fighter jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jet' looks like an aircraft, but it is a jet of liquid; take A out of SPRAY to get SPRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone, usually elderly, who is lively and nimble, so it is a synonym of active.

clue.text: Type of union formation that makes sparks fly

definitions.text: Type of union formation that makes sparks fly

blocks.clueFragment: Type of union formation that makes sparks fly
blocks.note: surface reading: setting up a trade union so militant that there is a row and tempers flare
setter's reading: a union is a join between two pieces of metal, made by a process that literally throws off sparks

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests workers and 'sparks fly' suggests a quarrel; both are literal in a metal workshop, where an electric arc fuses steel.
explanation.definitionFit: Arc welding joins metal using the heat of an electric arc, a process that sends showers of sparks into the air.

clue.text: Universal good name in airy quality, ignoring the initial belligerence

indicators.note: ignoring the initial means passing over the first letter of the word it follows
items placed in a word sit among its letters

blocks.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
G is the abbreviation for good
N is the abbreviation for name
a room with an airy quality has spaciousness

explanation.surface: A noble, well-regarded name in the world of light and air somehow carries an aggressive streak.
explanation.walkthrough: SPACIOUSNESS drops its S, and U, G and N go in after the P: P-UGN-ACIOUSNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pugnaciousness is an eagerness to fight or quarrel, the same aggressive disposition as belligerence.

clue.text: Olympic site secured by Pole in charge after cruel treatment?

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast within it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a ship's mast is a tall pole
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge
the Russian resort that hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics

explanation.surface: A Polish official runs an Olympic venue after a spell of harsh treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is not a Polish person but a ship's spar. Sochi hosted the 2014 Winter Olympics. 'after' means seeking, not following in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A masochistic person takes pleasure in pain, so they are literally after, meaning in pursuit of, cruel treatment.

clue.text: Eating fish, virile or not?

indicators.note: a word eating another takes it inside, so its letters surround the other

blocks.note: virile means manly
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A dieter wonders whether eating fish makes a man more virile.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: MANLY with a fish inside becomes its opposite, the 'or not' of virile.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenly means like a young girl, gentle and modest, the very opposite of virile masculinity.

clue.text: It’s wet and sticky topping of stewed fruit

indicators.note: in a down entry the topping of a word is its uppermost, first letter

blocks.note: first letter of the word
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A dessert of stewed fruit with a wet, gooey topping.
explanation.definitionFit: Slime is a moist, viscous substance, so the description of something both wet and sticky fits it.

clue.text: Open part of station training for swindlers?

blocks.note: a con is a swindle, the work swindlers do
a course is a programme of training

explanation.surface: A traveller hurries across the open hall of a railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay backwards: a training course for swindlers would be a CON COURSE. The question mark flags the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is the large open hall of a railway station where passengers gather before boarding trains.

clue.text: Harmonious arch

blocks.note: first meaning: in agreement, moving together, as marchers do
second meaning: the arched upper part of the foot

explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' looks like an adjective (sly) or an architectural feature; it is the curve of the foot. The first meaning is the two-word phrase IN STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in step means acting in harmony, and the instep is the arched middle part of the human foot.

clue.text: It’s too late to undo result of frying accident

annotation.answer: THE FAT IS IN THE FIRE

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for something irreversible that is bound to cause trouble
second meaning: what literally happens when grease spills from the pan into the flames

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is read literally for the second meaning: a chip pan spilling grease into the flames.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means the damage is done and trouble cannot be avoided; literally, spilled grease has reached the cooking flames.

clue.text: Dickensian character of police business?

blocks.note: copper is slang for a police officer
a field is a line of business or area of activity

explanation.surface: A detective in a Dickens novel goes about routine police work.
explanation.walkthrough: A copper's field is police business, read the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: David Copperfield is the narrator and hero of the Charles Dickens novel that bears his name.

clue.text: Requirement for telling computer how to detect orator’s plagiarism?

blocks.note: first meaning: the software that lets a machine understand spoken commands
second meaning, whimsical: spotting that a speaker's words have been heard before

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a pun: you catch a plagiarist by knowing the speech already, recognising it.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech recognition is technology that converts spoken words into commands a computer can act on, so you can talk to it.

clue.text: Recalled games with the woman leading mindless followers

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read back to front

blocks.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: A woman recalls the school games she led for a crowd of thoughtless followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' puts SHE in front of the reversed games.
explanation.definitionFit: People who follow the crowd unthinkingly are called sheep, after the flock animal that trails its leader.

clue.text: Unashamed sexy person’s trick

blocks.note: openly declared, as when someone is out about their sexuality
fox is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A shameless seducer plays a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To outfox someone is to outwit them by cunning, so it is a verb meaning to trick or outsmart.

clue.text: Winds blowing strongly through shelter seen in fine print?

indicators.note: blowing through something means passing inside it, so these letters run within the other word

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
gales are strong winds

explanation.surface: Strong winds rush past a shelter where a notice is pinned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing strongly' belongs with the gales in the surface; only 'through' is needed to put them inside LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Legalese is the dense jargon of legal documents, typically found in the small print of contracts, hence fine print.

clue.text: Some beware voyages, returning in dismay

indicators.note: some of a phrase means only a run of its letters is used
returning means going back, so the run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Some sailors fear sea voyages, coming home in despair.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe is to intimidate or subdue by inspiring fear, close in sense to the verb to dismay.

clue.text: Excited calf runs round a certain bird handler

indicators.note: an excited animal jumps about, so the letters that follow are scrambled
going round something means surrounding it, so the jumbled letters enclose the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
one means a certain, as in 'one day'

explanation.surface: A frisky calf circles a particular bird-keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a certain' reads as an adjective for the handler, but it stands for a word, as in 'a certain day' or 'one day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A falconer keeps and trains falcons or hawks for hunting, so they are a handler of birds of prey.

clue.text: Men only come again with one providing a change of scenery

definitions.text: one providing a change of scenery

blocks.note: a stag party is for men only
a request to repeat: 'eh?'
and means together with

explanation.surface: A men-only party asks someone to repeat themselves while a holiday-maker seeks new surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' does double duty as AND; the definition plays on 'change of scenery' meaning a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagehands move props and sets in a theatre between scenes, literally changing the scenery on stage.

clue.text: Rebellious BBC (not united) bash the monarch with space in roster

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for the word united is left out
placed in a word means set among its letters

blocks.note: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC
U is the abbreviation for united
to have a bash at something is to have a stab at it
HM, His or Her Majesty
an en is a printer's space
a roster is a list of names

explanation.surface: A rebellious broadcaster attacks the monarch and leaves a slot in its schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is nicknamed Auntie in Britain, and an en is a printer's space. 'bash' means an attempt, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anti-establishment means opposing the ruling powers and conventions of society, which is a rebellious stance.

clue.text: Head off scorn in public, maintaining America is fake

indicators.note: taking the head off a word removes its first letter
maintaining means holding, so the outer word keeps the other inside it

blocks.note: to pillory is to ridicule someone openly, as in the old public stocks
the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A critic heads off public scorn by insisting America is a sham.
explanation.walkthrough: The pillory was a wooden frame where offenders were exposed to public ridicule, hence the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illusory is deceptive and not real, appearing to exist when it does not, so it is fake.

clue.text: Short ditty, catch or verse

indicators.note: a short version of a word is missing its last letter

blocks.note: a ditty is a simple song
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A choice between a brief song, a round, or a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' can be a type of round song, which suits the surface; here it means to net.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem in a fixed rhyme scheme, so it is a piece of verse.

clue.text: Singer Joanna knocking out number loudly

indicators.note: knocking something out removes it, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang for piano
No. is the abbreviation for number
f, forte, is the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A singer called Joanna belts out a number at full volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joanna' looks like a woman's name; in Cockney rhyming slang it means a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Édith Piaf was the celebrated French singer known for chansons such as Non, je ne regrette rien.

clue.text: Statistical diagram segment mostly on deer

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a segment is a piece
a hart is a male red deer

explanation.surface: A chart showing what share of the deer population lives in each region.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie chart is a circular graph divided into slices, each showing a proportion of the data.

clue.text: Perhaps an aggressive dog is half-heartedly resentful

indicators.note: with only half its heart, the word loses one of its two middle letters

blocks.note: bitter means resentful

explanation.surface: A snappy dog may be only mildly resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER has a double T at its heart; dropping one of them halves the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that bites is a biter, and an aggressive dog is one example of something that bites.

clue.text: Perennial old shipwreck’s stern half has been raised

indicators.note: in a down entry the rear half lifted up moves above, to the front of, the rest

blocks.note: Henry VIII's warship the Mary Rose sank in 1545 and was raised from the seabed in 1982

explanation.surface: The back half of a famous old wreck has been lifted from the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: The wreck really was raised; here 'raised' moves ROSE above MARY in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an evergreen herb that lives for many years, so it is a perennial plant.

clue.text: General agreement has Office for National Statistics involved in this event

indicators.note: the answer with these letters involved in it makes the first word, so taking them out of that word leaves the answer

blocks.note: consensus is broad agreement
ONS is the abbreviation for the Office for National Statistics

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees that the national statistics office is involved in the event.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in reverse: 'this event' with ONS put in gives CONSENSUS, so remove ONS. The ONS runs the British census.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of the population, held as a periodic national event, and run by the statistics office.

clue.text: Faltering French of keen nurses

indicators.note: to nurse something is to hold it close, so one word cradles the other

blocks.note: keen in the sense of sharp, cutting
de is French for of

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic nurse speaks hesitant French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like a noun for medical staff but is a verb meaning holds; 'keen' is sharp, not eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone indecisive hesitates and cannot make up their mind, wavering just as a faltering person does.

clue.text: Reversing pieces for ludo and chess, sound as a bell

blocks.note: ludo is played with counters
a chess piece is called a man
ding is the sound a bell makes

explanation.surface: A set of game pieces for ludo and chess, all in perfect condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' is an idiom for in good condition; here it is the noise a bell makes. 'pieces for' serves both games.
explanation.definitionFit: To countermand an order is to revoke or cancel it, so countermanding means reversing a previous instruction.

clue.text: Not a good bet, dealing with grand service

blocks.note: evens odds pay back only your own stake
on, as in 'a book on birds'
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A gambler weighs up a poor bet on a grand scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, sung in cathedrals and churches towards the end of the day.

clue.text: In shifting dune, chumps note feline is wild

indicators.note: a shifting dune moves its sand about, so the word's letters change places
items in a word sit inside it, surrounded by its letters

blocks.note: taken as written
chump and dome are both slang for the head
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: Fools and a cat out on the shifting sand dunes have run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Chump and dome are both slang for the head, so chumps are domes. Ti is the sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: An undomesticated animal has never been tamed or kept as a pet, so it remains wild.

clue.text: Unimportant affair eclipses journey’s end

indicators.note: to eclipse something is to blot it out of view, so the letter at that point disappears

blocks.note: a trip is a journey
the final letter of the journey word, the one that gets covered
a fling is a brief affair

explanation.surface: A casual romance overshadows the end of a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: FLING covers the last letter of TRIP, leaving TRI-FLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifling describes something of little value or consequence, a synonym for unimportant or trivial.

clue.text: Something primarily gripped to protect one

definitions.text: Something primarily gripped to protect one

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter counts
protecting something means surrounding it, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: first letter of the word
gripped means held
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soldier grabs the first thing to hand to protect himself.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a knight's protective plate is held by a grip on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A shield is held in front of the body to ward off blows, exactly a thing gripped for self-protection.

clue.text: Changing out of uniform, shapeless, in allotment

indicators.note: something out of a word is missing from it, so that letter goes
a word put in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: amorphous means having no definite shape
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
meting out is allotting, so meting is an allotment

explanation.surface: A gardener changes out of a work uniform into scruffy clothes on the allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a rented garden plot in Britain, but here it is the act of allotting; U is uniform in the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Metamorphosing means undergoing a transformation, as a caterpillar does into a butterfly, so it means changing form.

clue.text: Inappropriately romanticise a deformity

indicators.note: done inappropriately means done wrongly, so the letters of the next word are wrongly ordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly glamorises a physical defect.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreation is something badly or wrongly formed, so it denotes a deformity or monstrous creation.

clue.text: One school in time to give up bond

indicators.note: things placed in a word sit inside its letters

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian season when people give things up
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A pupil gives up a school bond in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is not a place of learning but GAM, a group of whales.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is the fibrous tissue that binds bones together at a joint, a physical bond in the body.

clue.text: Branch operations?

blocks.note: surface reading: the business carried on at a bank's local branch offices
setter's reading: the limbs of a tree, cut and treated by an arborist

explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch' suggests a shop or bank office; the operations are performed on real tree branches.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree surgery is the pruning, felling and treating of trees, work carried out on their limbs by arborists.

clue.text: Merry man‘s description of smallest room in Vegas?

blocks.note: the smallest thing is described as little
john is American slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A cheerful man describes the tiniest bathroom in a Las Vegas hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smallest room' is a British euphemism for the toilet, which in America is the john.
explanation.definitionFit: Little John was the giant member of Robin Hood's band of outlaws, known as the Merry Men.

clue.text: I’m po-faced, therefore also smothering humour, ultimately

indicators.note: smothering something means covering it completely, so one word encloses the letter
ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is wanted

blocks.note: so means therefore
besides means also, in addition
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A solemn speaker admits they keep all humour firmly suppressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person: the answer describing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobersides is a humourless, solemn person, so the answer could say of itself that it is po-faced.

clue.text: Jerk hugged by Daniel, shivering just the same

indicators.note: something hugged by another is held within its arms, so it goes inside
a shivering body shakes, so the letters of the name are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: Daniel, shivering, hugs someone who is just as cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for a person; it is an involuntary twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike in every detail, so two identical things are just the same as each other.

clue.text: Cheerful, different note for start of abstinence

indicators.note: a different note for the start means the opening letter, itself a musical note, is swapped for another

blocks.note: G is one of the musical notes A to G
self-denial is going without, abstinence

explanation.surface: Someone becomes much happier on swapping a note at the start of a sober spell.
explanation.walkthrough: DENIAL begins with D, also a note; swapping it for G gives GENIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A genial person is friendly and good-humoured, with a warm manner, so genial is a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Wandering etc, touring West Indies repeatedly

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so they are rearranged
touring a place means travelling round it, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers keep roaming around the Caribbean islands, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: TWICE strictly means two times; 'repeatedly' is a loose but fair stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Twice means on two occasions, so it describes something done more than once, which is a fair sense of repeatedly.

clue.text: Basic upbringing of male child keeps father sick

indicators.note: in a down entry bringing a word up reads it from the bottom, so it is turned around
something that keeps others holds them inside it

blocks.note: a son is a male child
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A simple childhood: a boy nursing his ailing dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upbringing' sounds like child-rearing; in a down light it lifts SON to read NOS, which holds FR+ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-frills product or service has only the essentials and no extras, so it is plain and basic.

clue.text: Central power eradicated in quickfire attack

indicators.note: eradicated means wiped out, so that letter is removed from the word it is in

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for power, here the central letter of the other word
rapid means quick, as in rapid fire

explanation.surface: The central authority is wiped out in a swift surprise attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden armed incursion into enemy territory, so it is a kind of military attack.

clue.text: Tall drivers enjoy less of this winding road home

definitions.text: Tall drivers enjoy less of this

indicators.note: a winding road twists about, so the letters that follow are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tall motorists dislike the twisting drive back to the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Headroom is the vertical space above a seated person's head in a car, which tall people find in short supply.

clue.text: Tend to be dishevelled with hair covering shapeless garment

indicators.note: dishevelled things are messed up, so the word's letters are disordered
covering something means lying over it on both sides, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Hair tends to get messy when wearing a loose frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tend' looks like the verb of the surface sentence but is the fodder itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent dress is a loose, tent-shaped dress that hangs from the shoulders without a defined waist, hence shapeless.

clue.text: Rodents, evidence of very cold student accommodation?

blocks.note: a dorm, dormitory, is student housing
ice forms when it is very cold

explanation.surface: Ice in student rooms shows how cold the halls are.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice in the dorm is the 'evidence' of a freezing hall of residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small, mouse-like rodents famous for long hibernation, like the sleepy one at the Mad Hatter's tea party.

clue.text: Which thing’s going to said plant in Australia?

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words are judged by how they come out of the mouth

blocks.note: what'll is short for what will, asking which thing is going to happen

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is going to become of a certain Australian plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle is the common Australian name for acacia, and its golden bloom is the country's national flower.

clue.text: Really a menace, delaying the queen

indicators.note: delaying something makes it come later, so the letter is lifted out and put back further along

blocks.note: a threat is a menace
R, for Regina, means queen

explanation.surface: A real threat, holding up the Queen's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: In A THREAT the R comes third; delayed until next to last it spells AT HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart means fundamentally, in one's true nature, so it is used like really: 'at heart he's kind'.

clue.text: Disturbed and called into action

indicators.note: something put into a word goes inside it

blocks.note: a deed is an action
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Worried, someone phoned and was sent into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called into action' reads as one phrase meaning summoned; it must be split after 'called'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged means mentally unbalanced or thrown into disorder, both of which fit the sense of disturbed.

clue.text: Skipping gate, found one’s way around bed

indicators.note: skipping something means leaving it out, so those letters are dropped
turned around means facing the other way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to navigate is to find one's way

explanation.surface: Someone avoids a gate and finds a route round a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like part of 'found one's way around', but it is the signal to turn the remainder back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a low bed with a solid base and no headboard or footboard.

clue.text: Burns possibly making black marks all over, causing shock

indicators.note: making one thing into another means it is changed, so one letter becomes another
turned all over means flipped, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Robert is the first name of the Scottish poet Burns
B is the pencil abbreviation for black
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Burns leave black scars all over, causing a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' looks like injuries, but it is the poet; with B made into M, ROBERT becomes ROMERT, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a shaking movement, such as a small earthquake, so it is a physical shock or jolt.

clue.text: Ray‘s part in German Tannhäuser

indicators.note: a part in a phrase is a run of letters sitting inside those words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A singer called Ray takes a role in a German production of Wagner's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray looks like a singer's first name; it is the fish. 'Ray's' stands for 'Ray is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The manta is the largest species of ray, a flat fish with wide wing-like fins.

clue.text: A sign of injury in Wagner’s world

blocks.note: first meaning: a raised red mark on the skin left by a blow
second meaning: the German word for world, Wagner being German

explanation.walkthrough: Wagner signals German, the language of the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A welt is a ridge on the skin from a lash or blow, and Welt is the German word for world.

clue.text: Start off quite well, then pint makes you clumsy

indicators.note: with the start taken off, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: feeling fine means quite well
